report.source_text: Since the plasma hyperosmolality associated with urine hypoosmolality persisted, central diabetes insipidus was suspected and a water deprivation test was carried out. Based on copeptin levels during thirsting (copeptin t0–4.3 pmol/l; copeptin t7–4.2 pmol/l) and response to desmopressin, we diagnosed central diabetes insipidus (Table 1). The polyuria of up to 12 L / d was normalized during the following days by application of desmopressin.
report.temporal_cue: after day 5 and before day 22 after admission

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 49-year-old male presented with strong piercing headaches, photophobia, severe nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and general sickness. A brain MRI revealed a hemorrhagic sellar mass. Subsequent workup showed persistent plasma hyperosmolality associated with urine hypoosmolality. Central diabetes insipidus was diagnosed based on a water deprivation test, copeptin levels (t0–4.3 pmol/l; t7–4.2 pmol/l), and response to desmopressin. The patient experienced polyuria of up to 12 L/d, which was normalized by desmopressin. A follow-up MRI after 3 weeks showed consolidation of the hemorrhage with a regressive shift of the optic chiasm.

Follow-up MRI after 3 weeks showed consolidation of the hemorrhage with a regressive shift of the optic chiasm.
